newsitem.title: USA: Dole says he will pull upset, like Harry Truman.
newsitem.headline: Dole says he will pull upset, like Harry Truman.

text.p: Republican Bob Dole charged into the last lap of his longshot campaign on Wednesday with a prayer at the Lincoln Memorial, a blistering attack on President Bill Clinton's economic policy and a prediction he would pull a stunning upset like Harry Truman did in 1948.
With six days to go to the election, underdog Dole said Clinton's tax and slow-growth policy could lead to a recession.
At a rally in a New Orleans suburb of Kenner, Dole reminded the crowd that Democrat Truman came from far behind to defeat Republican Tom Dewey.
"Keep your eye on me -- I'm going to be a second Harry Truman," he shouted to wild applause.
And in an interview with television personality David Frost, the 73-year-old candidate would not concede he might lose, but said if he does it would be his last campaign.

"I'm not suggesting it's going to happen. But if it should happen I'll probably find work. I'll work with people with disabilities and I'll do other things fulfilling," said Dole, who has an impaired right arm from wounds from the Second World War.
"But I'm not going to go off and say it's all over. It's not over 'til it's over," said Dole, quoting one of baseball's legends. "Yogi Berra is one of my consultants."
Dole opened his day in Washington with a visit to the Lincoln Memorial for what he said was inspiration and a moment of silent prayer for the election just six days away.

Far behind in polls, Dole then flew to Clarksville, Tennessee, to hit Clinton head-on on one of the incumbent's strong points -- a steady, growing economy, low inflation, a booming stock market and low unemployment.
But Dole said Clinton's policies, including a 1993 tax hike, would put the economy into a deep slide.

"It doesn't take a team of economists to tell you what happens when you mix slow growth with tax hikes -- that's a recipe for economic collapse," said Dole in his prepared remarks. "Well, if he is re-elected, brace yourself for the Clinton recession."

In delivering the speech, he called the Clinton policy a "recipe for economic collapse" but veered some from his prepared text to follow with "if this is a recovery, I can hardly wait for the recession."

Dole, whose campaign has centred on an economic package and 15 percent income tax rate cut he said would produce a 3.5 percent economic growth rate, seized on Wednesday's government figures showing a 2.2 percent increase in the gross domestic product for the three months ending on Sept. 30.
"This is a real economic slowdown," Dole said, noting it had dropped from the second quarter growth rate.

"And it is disastrous news for American workers and businesses and even worse news for low and middle income Americans who haved been squeezed by lower wages and higher taxes," Dole said to a rally at Austin Peay State University in Clarksville, Tennessee.
Dole claimed his economic plan "is designed to steer the economic ship the other way. "
Dole was introduced by his wife; Elizabeth, who said Dole should be elected because "he is a better man for America."
